name: feature
description: Standard workflow for implementing a new product or engineering feature: pin the spec, break it down, build it in slices, prove it with tests, review it, then ship it when it is ready.

stages.purpose: Understand how the existing code behaves and what constraints it carries before changing anything.
Write down objectives, boundaries, and success criteria so the work has a fixed target.
Break the spec into ordered, independently verifiable tasks.
Land the work in thin slices, each one verifiable on its own.
Prove behaviour with tests written before the code that satisfies them.
Review the finished change across correctness, security, and maintainability before it merges.
Prepare the rollout only when the feature is actually going out.

rules: Complete each stage before treating it as complete.

The stage order is the shape of the work, not permission to implement everything before testing it: the test-driven-development discipline governs what happens inside each build slice, so the test for a slice comes before the code for that slice.
Carry verified findings forward into the next stage instead of re-deriving them.
Do not silently skip a required stage; a stage you could not complete is reported as blocked.
Do not claim verification that did not happen.
Keep the spec and the task list updated when the work changes shape.
completion: The feature is complete when the review stage passes and every claim in the final report is backed by a command that was actually run.
